Resolves #21662

Dragging a Ready card out of Workstation's Board and releasing it over the Scheduler could mark it Done. The Board now measures its own bounds and its columns at release. Dropping outside returns the card to its original position.

Evidence: L3. The Workstation tests drive a real pointer and read the shared work-item record back from the App Worker.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 · Off-board release | Crossing beneath Done and releasing over the Scheduler fires zero card moves. Status, order, resource and dates keep their original values. The same gesture moved the card to Done before the fix. |
| AC-2 · Re-entry and ordinary sorting | Re-entering the collapsed Done header commits once. The Board unit tests cover Escape with pointer coordinates, release into an empty column, and insertion between the two previewed neighbours. |
| AC-3 · Browser controls | Workstation checks the source record and the number of move events. A second gesture releases in a measured column gap and checks that the Scheduler bar shows the committed Board status. |

## Deltas from ticket

Gutters, padding and swimlane headers inside the Board preserve the slot shown in the last visible destination column. Their pointer height does not change the insertion order. If that column has scrolled entirely out of view, the card returns home. A direct column hit uses the release coordinates. Coordinate-free programmatic completion retains its accepted column. The new geometry helper is protected.

## Test Evidence

The gutter test failed on the first PR head. The move-phase test also failed under each regression independently. Horizontal-only hit testing entered Done from below the Board. Restoring the off-column vertical sort advanced the preview from slot 1 to slot 3.

174 Board unit tests and 32 headless Chromium tests passed across the basic Board, swimlanes and Workstation Planning.

## Post-Merge Validation

The Board, swimlane and Workstation regressions exercise the interaction before merge.

Authored by Sophie (GPT-6.2 Astra, reasoning: ultra, Codex Desktop). Session 00ac0a20-d01f-4bd1-a468-6725ed318723.
